body.en: DNA is enclosed within membranes, so cells are broken open with enzymes: lysozyme for bacteria, cellulase for plant cells and chitinase for fungi. DNA is bound to histones and mixed with RNA and proteins, so the extract is treated with ribonuclease to remove RNA and protease to remove proteins. Purified DNA finally precipitates on adding chilled ethanol and can be seen as a collection of fine threads in the suspension, which can be spooled out. The purified DNA is then incubated with a restriction enzyme under optimal conditions, and agarose gel electrophoresis checks the digestion. The vector DNA is cut with the same enzyme, and the "cut" source DNA and vector are mixed with DNA ligase to make recombinant DNA.

Every cycle doubles the target DNA, so n cycles give 2^n copies. An ordinary polymerase is destroyed by the first heating.

body.en: PCR (*polymerase chain reaction*) makes multiple copies of a gene (DNA of interest) in vitro, using two sets of primers (small chemically synthesised oligonucleotides complementary to the regions of DNA at the ends of the target) and DNA polymerase. Each cycle has three steps: denaturation (the double-stranded DNA is separated by high temperature), annealing (primers bind to the single strands) and extension (the polymerase extends the primers using the nucleotides provided and the DNA as template). A thermostable DNA polymerase, Taq polymerase from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus, survives the high denaturation temperature. Since every cycle doubles the DNA, repeating the process many times amplifies the segment approximately a billion times. The amplified fragment can be ligated into a vector for cloning.

tagline.en: Isolating DNA, amplifying genes by PCR, and scaling up product formation in bioreactors with downstream processing.

say.en: DNA is enclosed by membranes and walls, so cells are broken open with enzymes: lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant cells), chitinase (fungi). DNA is wrapped with histones and mixed with RNA, so ribonuclease removes RNA and protease removes proteins.

Purified DNA is cut with restriction enzymes and checked on agarose gel. The gene of interest is then amplified by the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), which uses two sets of primers (small chemically synthesised oligonucleotides complementary to the ends of the target region) and a thermostable DNA polymerase — Taq polymerase from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus.
The amplified gene is ligated into a vector and introduced into a competent host. If the host expresses the foreign gene, it makes a recombinant protein.

problem.en: A PCR starts with 1 molecule of double-stranded target DNA. Assuming perfect doubling, how many copies are present after 10 cycles, and after 30 cycles?

steps.en: Each cycle doubles the DNA: N = N₀ × 2ⁿ.

answer.en: 1,024 copies after 10 cycles; about 1.07 billion after 30 cycles.

say.en: Let us work through this together. A PCR starts with 1 molecule of double-stranded target DNA. Assuming perfect doubling, how many copies are present after 10 cycles, and after 30 cycles?
Each cycle doubles the DNA: N equals N 0 times 2 to the power n.
After 10 cycles: 2 to the power 10 equals 1,024 copies.
After 30 cycles: 2 to the power 30 equals 1,073,741,824 is approximately 1.07 times 10 to the power 9 copies.
So the answer is 1,024 copies after 10 cycles; about 1.07 billion after 30 cycles.

say.en: Let us work through this together. A sample begins with 50 copies of a gene. How many cycles are needed to reach at least 50,000 copies?
We need 50 times 2 to the power n is greater than or equal to 50,000, so 2 to the power n is greater than or equal to 1,000.
2 to the power 9 equals 512 is too small; 2 to the power 10 equals 1,024 is enough.
So n equals 10 cycles.
So the answer is 10 cycles (50 times 1,024 equals 51,200 copies).
